standard_prerequisites.name: Determinant of an endomorphism of a finite free module whose reduction modulo the ideal is the identity
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: used at proof lines 107-109; the same fact is packaged in the hypothesis that every element of 1 + I is a unit
standard_prerequisites.use: The determinant of the lifted composite is congruent to 1 modulo I and is therefore invertible, so the lifted composite is itself invertible; that invertibility is what makes the sequence 0 -> Ker(phi) -> R^m -> R^n -> 0 split.

standard_prerequisites.name: Finitely generated projective modules over a ring and the splitting of short exact sequences of projective modules
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: the chapter's own remark at source lines 66-67 that a stably free module is projective
standard_prerequisites.use: Makes the kernel of the split surjection phi a direct summand of the finite free module R^m, hence finite stably free.

standard_prerequisites.name: Stable freeness and stable isomorphism of modules over a ring
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: the chapter's own Definition definition-stably-free at source lines 53-64, which fixes the meaning of the terms used in the statement
standard_prerequisites.use: Fixes the class of modules being lifted: E is finite stably free over R/I and the constructed M must be finite stably free over R with M/IM isomorphic to E.

core_obligations: Turn the hypothesis that E is finite stably free over R/I into a concrete isomorphism E + (R/I)^n = (R/I)^m for explicit n and m, so that the problem becomes a lifting problem for maps between free modules (proof lines 101-102).

Build R-linear lifts phi : R^m -> R^n and psi : R^n -> R^m of the projection and of the injection appearing in that isomorphism, and observe that the composite phi o psi reduces to the identity modulo I (proof lines 103-108).

Use the hypothesis on I through the determinant of phi o psi to show that the composite is invertible rather than merely congruent to the identity modulo I; this step consumes the Jacobson radical hypothesis and cannot be replaced by Nakayama alone (proof lines 108-109).

Conclude that the sequence 0 -> Ker(phi) -> R^m -> R^n -> 0 splits, so that M = Ker(phi) is a direct summand of a finite free module and therefore stably free, and verify that M/IM is the given E (proof lines 110-111).
proof_roadmap: Choose n, m and an isomorphism E + (R/I)^n = (R/I)^m witnessing stable freeness of E (proof lines 101-102).
Lift the projection (R/I)^m -> (R/I)^n and the injection (R/I)^n -> (R/I)^m to R-linear maps phi : R^m -> R^n and psi : R^n -> R^m (proof lines 103-106).
Show that phi o psi reduces to the identity modulo I, so that its determinant lies in 1 + I and is a unit by hypothesis; hence phi o psi is invertible (proof lines 107-109).
Conclude that phi is split surjective with finite stably free kernel M = Ker(phi), and that M/IM is the given E (proof line 110).
difficulty_reason: The lemma lifts a finite stably free module E over R/I to a finite stably free module over R itself when I lies in the Jacobson radical (statement lines 94-97). The proof first replaces E by an explicit isomorphism E + (R/I)^n = (R/I)^m, then has to choose two R-linear lifts phi and psi of the corresponding projection and injection (proof lines 101-106), and to prove that the composite phi o psi, which is only congruent to the identity modulo I, is actually invertible: this is done by inspecting its determinant, which lies in 1 + I and is therefore a unit by the hypothesis on I (proof lines 107-109). The last step reads the kernel of the split surjection phi off as a direct summand of a finite free module, hence stably free, and checks that it reduces to E (proof lines 110-111). The non-routine ingredient is the determinant argument, which upgrades a congruence modulo I to genuine invertibility without any locality or Nakayama input; nothing beyond the two reductions is cited.
